texts.preamble: Master Rohan vs Sh. Sahib Singh on 1 November, 2022 :1: In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi This Is One Of The 20 Oldest Matters Pending In This Tribunal, Hence Taken On Priority Basis. Mact No.: 137/17 Cnr No.: Dlse01-001281-2017 Master Rohan S/o Sh. Ashok Singh R/o H.No. 5/24, Dakshin Puri Extension, New Delhi-110062. .....Petitioner Versus 1. Sh. Sahib Singh S/o Sh. Samey Singh R/o H.No. 145, Mundka, New Delhi. .....Driver/Respondent no.1 2. M/s. Antony Road Transport Solution Pvt. Ltd. Transport Department of Delhi Bus Cluster no. 7 Project, Near Tharmal Plant Rajghat Depot-11, New Delhi. .......Owner/Respondent no.2 3. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. New India Assurance Building, 87 M.G. Road Fort, Mumbai. ............Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Mact No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 1 of 25 Bk Date of accident : 17.12.2016 Date of filing of Dar : 14.02.2017 Date of Decision : 01.11.2022 Award 1.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 14.02.2017 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. But it is further noted that as per record, my Ld. Predecessor noted in ordersheet dated 16.03.2017 that a independent claim petition u/s 166 of MV Act dated 14.02.2017 itself is also filed by the petitioner through Ld. Counsel and same was tagged with the DAR, as per such order dated 16.03.2017. 3. Brief facts of the case are that on 17.12.2016 at about 2.30 AM, petitioner/injured was returning home from his school with his friends and when he was about to board the offending "DTC bus", as per the petition, filed by petitioner, at Lodhi Colony, New Delhi, petitioner was badly hit and fell under the bus by the sudden starting and speeding of bus negligently by R-1 who was driving such bus bearing no. DL-1PD-2324. As a result, petitioner fell down on the road and the tyre of offending vehicle passed over and crushed the legs and other parts of the petitioner beside causing severe injuries to petitioner. Petitioner was referred to Batra hospital, Delhi for treatment and operation after first aid initially from AIIMS Trauma Center. It is further stated that injured was a bachelor and minor at the time of accident aged about 16 years only. It is further claimed that he MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 2 of 25 BK was a school going student. It is further stated that because of such rash and negligent act of respondent no.1, petitioner also suffered permanent injury and as such loss of future prospects. 4. Accordingly the FIR in question u/s 279/338 IPC was registered in this case and even chargesheet is filed. 5. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 12.05.2020 noticing 15% permanent physical impairment in relation to his both upper limbs and left lower limbs. 6. Further, as per record, initially Sahib Singh/R-1 as well as one Kuldeep Gola for R-2/owner company appeared. But they stopped appearing thereafter. In fact, their right to file WS was subsequently closed vide order dated 26.10.2017. 7. But reply filed by insurance company/R-3. In nutshell, in such reply, it is stated that the injured/petitioner suffered injuries due to his own negligence and he is responsible solely for the accident in question. It is further claimed that petitioner was boarding a moving bus and as such fell down and run over by the bus. Thus, it is further submitted that at least there is contributory negligence on the part of petitioner himself. It is further stated that offending bus is a cluster bus bearing no. DL-1PD-2324 in the name of M/s. Antony Road Transport Solution Pvt. Ltd. 8. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 26.10.2017 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 17.01.2016 (should be 17.12.2016) due to rash and negligent driving of MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 3 of 25 BK vehicle no. DL-1PD-2324 (DTC bus)(the same should be "cluster bus")being driven by R1 & owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP. Master Rohan vs Sh. Sahib Singh on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155828224/ 2 2. whom?OPP 3. Relief. 9. Further, as per record vide order dated 05.07.2018 present case was adjourned sin-e-die by my learned Predecessor as adjournment was sought again at that time to lead evidence stating that petitioner is still undergoing medical treatment and is not in a position to move. Further, liberty was given to the petitioner to get the present petition revived as and when petitioner recovers from injury and the file was consigned to record room. 10. Thereafter, as per record it appears that matter was revived from 21.09.2020. Further, as per record, vide order dated 02.08.2021, my learned predecessor noted that petitioner shall not be entitled to interest from 05.07.2018 till 21.09.2020. 11. Further, as per record, Petitioner Master Rohan examined himself as PW-1. Such PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/X. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/A till Ex. PW-1/E. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3. 12. Further, such petitioner got examined one Piyush as PW-2, alleging that he is his friend and an eye witness to the incident in question. Such Piyush is also cross-examined by counsel for insurance company. MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 4 of 25 BK 13. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 14. Further, as per record, None of the respondent led any evidence. Master Rohan vs Sh. Sahib Singh on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155828224/ 3 18. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. Page No. 5 of 25 BK investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. , PW-1/injured deposed that he did not tell the doctors of Trauma center about his accident as he was in unconscious condition. Further, he deposed that he remained in semi-conscious condition for about 2-3 days but he do not know whether he filed any documents in support thereof.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. 19. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. Thus, it is argued by learned counsel for insurance company that it is an independent noting/observation recorded immediately after the accident and as such, based on the same, it is clear that there is at least contributory negligence of the petitioner/injured himself. As such, in the peculiar facts Master Rohan vs Sh. Sahib Singh on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155828224/ 4 and circumstances of the case, it is held that no contributory negligence is proved on record on part of the petitioner. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 8 of 25 BK 26. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Master Rohan vs Sh. Sahib Singh on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155828224/ 5 Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 26.1. 26.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 9 of 25 BK (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 26.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 26.7. 27. What requires to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 10 of 25 BK standard multiplier method used to determine loss of dependency). 28. This means that the Tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence: Master Rohan vs Sh. Sahib Singh on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155828224/ 6 (i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary; (ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement; (iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,that is, the permanent disability suffered by the person. 29. In Judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as "M. R. Krishna Murthi vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. on 5 March, 2019, (2020) 15 SCC 493: (2020) 4 SCC (Crl.) 84: 2019 SCC Online SC 315, after dealing with various case laws relating to injury matters and death cases in case of students, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows: MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 11 of 25 BK 24. In those cases where the victim of the accident is not an earning person but a student, while assessing the compensation for loss of future earning, the focus of the examination would be the career prospect and the likely earning of such a person in future. That can be the future earning. In case MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 12 of 25 BK of death of victim, it would result in total loss of earning. In this background, it is claimed by learned counsel for insurance company that there is no "loss of income" at present and further there is no loss of future prospect. It is further pointed out that normally in MACT claim, under other various heads, other than these two, suitable compensation can be given as per law. It is further argued that as permanent disability is only 15% relating to both upper limbs and left lower limb, there is no functional disability also. On the other hand, it is argued by learned counsel for petitioner that at least there is 15% permanent functional disability in the present case having regard to material on record and accordingly compensation be given for future prospect. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". The expression used in guideline No. (iv) issued by this Court is that in the case of literate persons MACT No. 137/17 Master Rohan v. Sahib Singh & Ors. Page No. 19 of 25 BK also the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i), whereas in the guideline Nos. (i), (ii), (iii) and (v), the expression used is that the Tribunal should. Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in Master Rohan vs Sh.
